name: Ayar Labs TeraPHY Optical I/O Chiplet
bandwidth_basis: PER OPTICAL PORT, PER DIRECTION. Ayar Labs product specification states: '8 full-duplex optical ports', '16 WDM transceiver slices per optical port', and '512 Gbps per port (4 Tbps per chiplet)', with total chiplet bandwidth given verbatim as '8 Tbps bi-directional'. 512 Gbps per full-duplex port converts to 512 / 8 = 64 GB/s per port in each direction. Total chiplet unidirectional throughput is 4 Tbps (= 500 GB/s per direction), and bidirectional aggregate is 8 Tbps (= 1,000 GB/s bidirectional aggregate across all 8 ports). Optical modulation is NRZ without forward error correction (FEC) requirements.
topology: In-package optical I/O chiplet tiled alongside compute dies via UCIe standard package electrical interface. Directly drives single-mode fibers across distances from millimeters to kilometers (package-to-package scale-up domain extension).
switching: Passive optical I/O powered by external SuperNova multi-wavelength continuous-wave (CW) laser source. Contains on-chip configurable crossbar mapping electrical UCIe channels to optical ports; no packet switching or protocol termination inside the optical engine itself.
notes: TeraPHY is Ayar Labs' monolithic electronic-photonic optical I/O chiplet fabricated on standard GlobalFoundries CMOS silicon photonics processes. Designed to be co-packaged or 2.5D/3D integrated with GPUs, TPUs, and custom AI accelerators via standard UCIe die-to-die interfaces.\n\nINFERENCE RELEVANCE: Large-scale LLM inference (particularly autoregressive decode with large batch sizes, or massive MoE models requiring all-to-all expert routing across thousands of chips) is throttled by copper trace reach and serializer/deserializer (SerDes) power. Copper NVLink and PCIe direct-attach cables are physically limited to ~1 meter without bulky, power-hungry active electrical cables (AEC) or retimers. TeraPHY delivers 10 ns latency per chiplet (excluding optical flight time in fiber) and sub-pJ/bit energy consumption, allowing multi-rack clusters to scale tensor-parallel and pipeline-parallel domains across distances of millimeters to kilometers at scale-up latencies. By decoupling physical proximity from scale-up domain boundaries, optical I/O enables distributed LLM inference clusters to treat rack-scale or multi-rack accelerator pools as a single coherent memory and compute fabric without the latency overhead of conventional multi-hop Ethernet/InfiniBand networks.
